correctness.rationale: For g_d(u)=P(s-u)+Hu^(d-1)(1-u), differentiating yields g_d'=-P+H[(d-1)u^(d-2)(1-u)-u^(d-1)]<0, since (d-1)u^(d-2)(1-u)<=1 and H<P; g_d(s)>0 and g_d(1)<0 give a unique stable equilibrium u_d. Its root equation and maximum of u^(d-1)(1-u) first bound u_d-s=O(1/d), then O(q^(d-1)) for fixed q in (s,1), permitting asymptotic (u_d-s)/s^(d-1)→H(1-s)/P. Taylor expanding the moving squared-radius level yields its shift. Reciprocal velocity subtraction is pointwise positive for each d, with endpoint integral from u0 to fixed t giving D t^(d-1)/(d-1); the moving interval has length of order s^(d-1) and contributes C s^(d-1), dominating because t<s. The constants were checked against F0(t)=Pt(s-t), and boundary assumptions ensure positive target/denominators. Universal claims are rigorous real-variable asymptotics.
